topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and progression models
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by outlining learning outcomes, tumor progression models, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt signaling cascades drive autonomous cellular proliferation.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired terminal differentiation maintains progenitor-like states in both hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the molecular mechanisms and regulatory balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins that allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, cellular senescence, and growth-control summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms of telomere maintenance and senescence bypass that enable unlimited replicative potential before concluding the section on growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine altered cancer metabolism, focusing on aerobic glycolysis and the role of metabolic mutations in generating oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It details how growing tumors activate the angiogenic switch to stimulate new blood vessel formation for nutrient and oxygen supply.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the sequential steps, selective barriers, and genomic features underlying the metastatic spread of cancer cells.

topics.label: Lecture summary and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with final reflections on cancer hallmarks, suggestions for further reading, and closing remarks.
